title: Generative design and screening produced experimentally tested antimicrobial QACs
summary: A topology-aware generative workflow and activity predictor prioritized quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs) for synthesis and testing. Across two workflows the authors report 29 selected compounds characterized and 11 QACs designated as novel, with measured minimum inhibitory concentrations of 1–32 μM against bacterial pathogens. Earlier same-team conference disclosures had already described AI-generated QAC design and synthesis; this record covers the later paper’s bounded tested results and does not claim the first AI-generated QACs or universal chemical novelty. Activity and cytotoxicity remain assay-specific and do not establish clinical use.
ai_technology: Topology-aware QAC generative model with structure/activity prediction and filtering (Q-HERO)
organization: George Mason University; Villanova University; Emory University; Saint Joseph’s University

source_review.scope: Primary ACS indexed full article, publication history, methods/results, named affiliations and indexed supporting-information description; earlier team conference disclosures as identified in the frozen source review.

evidence.tested: The article reports synthesis and antimicrobial testing across two workflows, with 29 selected compounds characterized and 11 reported novel QACs with MIC values of 1–32 μM.
evidence.unknown: Prior same-team AI-QAC design and synthesis were described in 2022 and 2024 institutional conference abstracts. The measured activity is limited to the reported laboratory assays and does not establish clinical efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: A topology-aware generative model proposed QAC structures, and learned activity filtering helped prioritize candidates for synthesis and antimicrobial assays.
